Add rate-limiting middleware to the API

Objective

Add request rate-limiting middleware to the Express API that enforces 100 requests per minute per IP address and returns a 429 response with a Retry-After header when the limit is exceeded.

Context

The API currently has no rate limiting. During a load test last week, abusive clients caused a cascading failure in the database connection pool. We need a sliding-window rate limiter at the middleware layer before any route handlers run.

Steps

  1. Install express-rate-limit
    Why: Provides a battle-tested sliding-window limiter with minimal setup.
    Verify
    node -e "require('express-rate-limit')" exits 0; package appears in package.json dependencies.
  2. Create src/middleware/rateLimiter.ts with a 100 req/min window configured for IP-based keying.
    Why: Isolating the middleware in its own file keeps app.ts clean and makes the limiter independently testable.
    Verify
    File exists; TypeScript compiles without errors; exported function accepts an Express RequestHandler interface.
  3. Register the middleware in src/app.ts before the first router.use call.
    Why: Must intercept all routes; registering before route handlers ensures no request bypasses the limiter.
    Verify
    app.ts imports rateLimiter and calls app.use(rateLimiter) before any app.use(router) line.
  4. Write unit tests in src/middleware/__tests__/rateLimiter.test.ts
    Why: Validates the limiter allows requests under the threshold and rejects with 429 over it, and confirms the Retry-After header is present.
    Verify
    npm test -- rateLimiter passes; coverage shows all limiter branches hit.

Tests

Objective-verification test

File: src/middleware/__tests__/rateLimiter.test.ts

Asserts: Requests 1–100 succeed with 200; request 101 returns 429 with Retry-After header.

Run: npm test -- rateLimiter

Acceptance Criteria

Verification

Start the server locally. Use ab -n 120 -c 10 http://localhost:3000/api/health. Requests 1–100 should respond 200; the remaining requests should respond 429 with a Retry-After header present in the response.
